provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The emitted program works on the grid as it is shown. Colour roles are fixed constants: corner = palette[0], 1-line = palette[1], 2-line = palette[2], background = palette[8].

1. It finds the corner holding the corner colour, scoring candidates by how well their row and column match the 1-line and 2-line colours. It then decides whether the 1-line is the row or the column through that corner.
2. It ignores those two lines and collects non-background cells. Lanes are maximal runs of rows (or columns) parallel to the 1-line, sorted nearest the 1-line first. Within each lane, blocks are maximal runs along the lane, sorted nearest the 2-line first. Each block is cut straight from the shown grid.
3. The original rule turns the scene counter-clockwise when its 1-line was vertical. A 90-degree turn swaps horizontal and vertical, so the original line was vertical exactly when (the shown 1-line is a column) XOR (d4 has an odd number of quarter turns). In that case only each block is turned locally. Conjugating counter-clockwise by the D4 map gives counter-clockwise for pure rotations and clockwise for the mirrored variants (d4 >= 4). Otherwise blocks are copied as they are.
4. The factory maps the original output's stacking direction (downward) and width direction (rightward) through the D4 map. That tells it which shown axis blocks stack along, whether the first block goes at the start or the end, and which way the width axis runs. Each block is centred across the longest block length. The floor or ceil of the centring offset is chosen to match the mirrored direction, although lengths are always even, so the two are equal.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Assumes the generator's domain: the two border lines through the corner, the background-only opposite borders, lanes separated by at least one background line, and blocks separated by at least one background cell with no background cells inside a block.
- A corrupted or missing corner cell is handled by a fallback based on colour counts.
- No contradictions with a single uniform rule were found in the fixtures.
- The demonstrations are not used, since the roles come from the palette and d4.
- I have not run any tests on this factory.
